images.filename: Tralee from the International Space Station 2013-03-17.jpg
images.caption:
"Tralee, Ireland, nestled in the first green we see after soaring across the Atlantic." – Caption by astronaut Chris Hadfield on board the International Space Station.
This is one of a set of eight pictures of Ireland taken from earth orbit that were posted on the internet by Hadfield to celebrate Saint Patrick's Day in 2013.

Tralee, the largest town in County Kerry (population 23,700), on the west coast of Ireland is in the centre of the picture, with the Slieve Mish Mountains immediately south, extending westwards into the Dingle Peninsula. The low mountains to the northeast of Tralee are the Stack's Mountains.

images.caption:
Scotia's Grave A path leads up beside the Finglas rivulet to the stones. It is reputed to be the grave of a daughter of an Egyptian Pharaoh in Glenn Scoithin, the vale of the little flower.
According to medieval Irish mythology Scotia, wife of the former Milesius and mother of six sons, was killed in battle with the legendary Tuatha Dé Danann on the nearby Slieve Mish mountain. Scotia had come to Ireland to avenge the death of her husband, the King who had been wounded in a previous ambush in south Kerry.
She was an accomplished horsewoman, but, while pregnant, attempted to jump a bank that would not normally have presented a problem. However, the extra mass of her pregnancy caused her to fall and die.
Ref Wikipedia for description

I assume this is the right stone as the somewhat overgrown path seemed to go no further.

images.filename: Tralee - Town dog reading sign on door of hat store - geograph.org.uk - 1633822.jpg
images.caption: Tralee - Town dog reading sign on door of hat store Up to this point in time, I've had a lot of respect for Ireland's town dogs, as they very well mannered, even though unleashed and on their own. After seeing this dog reading the sign on the door of this hat store, my respect has only grown. I suspect the owner is inside this hat store shopping. I also suspect that this dog just might understand the sign, which states "Management Reserves the Right to Refuse Admission". Ireland's town dogs truly amaze me.
